newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan's king rebukes Israel's Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king rebukes Israel's Netanyahu.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein wrote to Benjamin Netanyahu saying he didn't trust the Israeli leader and warning of an impending explosion of the Middle East peace process, Israeli newspapers reported on Tuesday.
"There was a certain letter we received in recent days. That's correct," Netanyahu's foreign policy adviser Dore Gold told Israeli army radio without elaborating.
The king, who signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994, was quoted by the Maariv newspaper as writing to Netanyahu: "You are destroying the peace, and I haven't an ounce of trust in you."
The rival newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth reported the king had warned of an "explosion of the peace process" unless Netanyahu reversed his plans to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Netanyahu, on an official visit to Moscow, was quoted by army radio as telling reporters: "There is no place for this criticism, certainly there is no place for this tone. There must be stability in statements."

Palestinians are angry at Israeli government decisions to build the new settlement and to hand over only a third of the West Bank land they had expected in an Israeli troop redeployment due to have taken place last week.
"This letter perhaps reflects the reality of our relations with Jordan -- that is our relations are very sensitive to what happens on the Palestinian track," Gold said.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai arrived in Jordan on Tuesday for talks with King Hussein on the troubled peace moves.
Mordechai held crisis talks on Monday night with Palestinian cabinet minister Yasser Abed Rabbo over Israel's unilateral plans for troop redeployment in the West Bank.
Netanyahu had written a letter back to the king, Israeli cabinet secretary Danny Naveh said.

Naveh also confirmed the king had been barred from flying Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to self-ruled Gaza after a meeting in Amman this week -- another subject which Israeli newspapers said the monarch complained about in the letter.

The Israeli cabinet secretary said the king could not fly to Gaza because Israel and the Palestinians were still locked in negotiations that would enable the Palestinians to operate an air strip in the self-ruled strip.
